blocks.text:
I'm noting the coordinates of the glucose-like ligand's carbon and oxygen atoms so I can identify which residues fall within 4 Å of them.

Checking TYR A18's ring atoms against the ligand, I find OH comes within roughly 2.8-3.5 Å of both C1 and O1, putting this residue clearly within range. I'm now moving to check HIS A22's side chain coordinates for similar proximity.

I trace HIS22's imidazole atoms and find NE2 sits about 3.06 Å from O5, confirming this residue is also within contact distance. Moving on, I check PRO24 and ILE25, both of which end up too far away, then continue to LEU29's delta carbons against C6, landing right at the edge around 4.0 Å.

I verify LEU29 falls just within range via CD2, but its other atoms (CD1, CG) are too far, so only CD2 counts. Next I check LEU33's delta carbons and TYR41's CB, but they all end up slightly beyond the cutoff, so I move on to scanning VAL67's side chain coordinates.

I start working through residues systematically for atoms near the (1.5, 2.5, 0) region, checking MET8's sulfur and carbon atoms against several C and O positions of the ligand, but each distance comes out just over 4 Å, ruling it out. I confirm HIS22 and TYR18 are already counted, then check TRP64 and LEU52, both too far in y and z, before moving to examine TRP76's ring carbons.

Checking TRP76's NE1 and CD1 atoms against several ligand oxygens and carbons, I find NE1-O5 and CD1-O2 distances both under 4 Å, confirming TRP76 as a contact. I then check TRP77, finding CD1-O3, NE1-O3 distances also qualify, so TRP77 joins the list, and I move on to check its CZ2 atom next.

Now I'm scanning through nearby residues -- TYR79, MET80, CYS73, VAL67, GLU28, ARG21, MET84, LEU52 -- calculating their closest atom distances to the ligand oxygens, but none fall within the 4 Å cutoff. HIS22's CD2 atom does qualify at around 3.66 Å, so I'm adding it, and I'm now checking ILE25's CG2 atom next.

Continuing through the residue list systematically, I'm checking MET8, TYR18, GLN19, ARG21, ILE25, LEU29, LEU33, TYR41, LEU52, MET84, TRP76, TRP77, VAL67, HIS36, and CYS73 against the ligand's oxygen and carbon positions -- so far only TRP76, TRP77, LEU29, and HIS22 are landing within range, everything else is too far. I'm moving on to check MET55 and TRP64 next.

But rechecking TYR41 more carefully, its hydroxyl oxygen (OH) actually comes out to about 3.45 Å from C3, which puts it within range after all -- so I need to walk through all the TYR41 ring atoms against the nearby ligand carbons and oxygens to confirm which ones qualify.

TYR41's CZ and OH both land within 4 Å of C4 and O4, so this residue is definitely part of the contact set -- I clearly need to be more thorough. I'm going to restart with a systematic bounding-box approach across all ligand atom coordinates to catch anything else I might have missed.

Now I'm working through each protein residue in order, checking if any atom falls inside the box (MET1, ILE2, ARG3 are all too far in y; starting to check LYS4's backbone and side chain atoms against the y-range cutoff).

Checking CE2's coordinates against the box boundary, it falls inside, so I'm now measuring its distance to the nearest ligand atom, starting with O3.

VAL7 doesn't seem close either. Checking MET8 distances too - SD to C2 comes out around 4.23, and CE to C1 works out to about 4.53, still not close enough.

Moving on to GLN9, its CB and N atoms are all too far out in z or x to be relevant.

For VAL10 relative to ASP46, most atoms land too negative in z or y, so I'm running through its coordinates to confirm nothing qualifies.

Continuing systematically through ASN11, LYS47, PRO12, ASP13, ALA14, HIS15, GLU16, and GLU17 — checking their z-coordinates against the target range, and each one falls outside the box (roughly -8 to -18), so none of these residues are close enough to matter.

Then I hit TYR18, which finally has atoms landing inside the box: OH, CZ, CE1, and CE2 all fit, though CD1 falls just outside the z-cutoff, and I'm checking CD2 next.

Continuing further, most of those side-chain atoms miss the box, but the OH-O1 distance confirms TYR18 is in. GLN19 and ARG20 fall entirely outside the box on the x and z axes, and ARG21 also has most atoms outside on the x-coordinate.

Checking HIS22 now, I'm finding NE2 close enough to O5 (3.06 Å) to count it as a contact, so I'm continuing to check its other atoms against nearby ligand atoms.

ASN23 and PRO24 both fail the x-coordinate cutoff entirely, so I'm ruling them out quickly. Moving to ILE25, its N atom is also out of range, so I'm checking the CA atom next.

Checking LEU29 atoms against the box bounds - CA is just barely out at z, but CB falls inside. I'm computing distances from CB, CG, CD1 to C6, and none come close enough to be a match.

CD2 checks out though - its distance to C6 comes to about 3.987, just under the 4.0 threshold, so LEU29 is included, if barely. Now I'm moving on to GLU30, checking CB and CG coordinates against the box, and CB doesn't fit.

ALA31, VAL32, and LEU33 all mostly fall outside the z-boundary of the box, with most atoms exceeding 6.55 or 10 depending on the residue. LEU33's CG lands inside the box but its distance to C6 comes out to about 5.14, too far, while CD1 checks in closer at around 4.06.

Checking further residues—LYS34, SER35, HIS36, GLY37, ALA38—their x, y, and z coordinates all fall outside the target box, ruling them out quickly.

Then HIS39 and ASN40 also get excluded for the same reason. TYR41 is the one that passes: its OH, CZ, and CE2 atoms all fall within the box and their computed distances to O4 satisfy the cutoff, so I'm including TYR41.

Moving to ALA42, every checked atom (N, CA, CB, C, O) lies outside the box bounds, so ALA42 is excluded. For ILE43, most atoms are out of range, though CD1 lands just inside the box with a distance of roughly 4.06 to C1, which is borderline enough to warrant a closer look.

Checking the distance from C1 to CD1 of ILE43 confirms roughly 4.06, so it's right at the edge but still within range.

Double-checking LEU29 CD2 distance to C6 more carefully: recomputing the differences gives about 3.987, which confirms it's just under 4.

Continuing the scan, I'm ruling out residues TYR44 through LEU51 since their coordinates fall well outside the relevant range in y or z. Moving to LEU52, I'm checking its backbone and sidechain atoms against the cutoff, finding N and CB both outside range, while CG needs further evaluation.

Checking LEU52's remaining atoms CD1 and CD2, both fall outside the pocket. PHE53's atoms are also too far in y, and ALA54's CB and CA are similarly out of range, so I'm continuing to rule out these residues one by one.

Moving through MET55, VAL56, and GLU57-59, none have atoms within the box range. SER60 and GLU61 are also excluded, but TRP64's CZ2 atom at (-1.785,-1.595,5.417) actually falls within the pocket boundaries, so that's a hit worth noting.

Checking CG1 distance again confirms it's too far. Continuing to scan ALA68 through VAL72 residues, computing z-coordinates and distances for their side chain atoms against O4 — none fall within range.

Moving to CYS73, I check its backbone and SG atoms against the box boundaries, then compute SG's distance to nearby oxygens O3 and O4 — both come out too far (5.57Å and 5.83Å). GLN74's atoms also fall outside the y-coordinate range, ruling it out too.

For TRP76, I'm checking each ring atom's distance to nearby ligand atoms: CD1, NE1, CE2, and CZ2 all fall within range of O2 and O5, while CB, CG, CD2, and CE3 are too far away.

Confirming TRP77 as included since CD1's distance to O2 also checks out under 4 Å. Moving on, I rule out LYS78 based on its y-coordinate range, and start checking TYR79's CB and CG atoms next.

Turning to MET80, I compute distances for each atom sequentially—N and CA fall outside the box, but CB's y-coordinate lands inside; its distance to O1 exceeds the 5 Å threshold though. CG comes in at roughly 4.66 Å from O1, and now I'm computing its distance to O5.

Checking the other distance for that atom confirms it's beyond the cutoff, so MET80 stays included based on the CE-O1 distance. Let me verify the CE coordinates against the PDB record to make sure I'm reading them correctly.

Then I continue scanning subsequent residues THR81 through MET84, checking each atom's coordinates against the cutoff range, but all of these fall outside the distance threshold on either the y or z axis.

Checking CE further out to no avail, so MET84 is ruled out. Moving to PRO85, checking CD coordinates but still nothing in range. Then scanning ALA86's CB, CA, and N atoms, but all fall outside the y or x bounds, so that residue is out too, and now I'm moving into ASN87's coordinates.

Checking CD's distance to O3 gives roughly 4.07, close but not quite matching; testing other nearby atoms like C2, C3, and O2 against the same reference point, but none of these distances land close enough either.

Weighing all these atom-distance pairs, PRO92 comes out with the smallest minimum at 4.07, which puts it outside the cutoff, so I'm going back to recheck the CG-to-O3 distance calculation for PRO92 more carefully.

Moving to VAL93, I'm checking each of its atoms against the reference point — CB, CG2, and N all fall outside the range, so I'll keep scanning through the remaining atoms.

SER94's CB and OG also fall outside the cutoff, and SER95 onward drifts further away in the x-coordinate. GLU96 through PRO104 are similarly too distant, so I want to circle back and recheck residues in the 60s-70s plus the N-terminal region for anything I might have missed.

Going through GLY37, HIS39, ALA42, ILE43, VAL56, PHE53, TYR18, HIS22, CYS73, TRP76, GLN74, LEU29, VAL67, and ALA54/PHE6 - none of their atoms land within the box. I'm now checking MET80's other atoms since only CE was close before.

Continuing, I check TYR79 OH, ARG21 NE, HIS22 CB - none qualify. This narrows my final list down to A:Y18, A:H22, A:L29, A:Y41, A:W76, A:W77, A:M80, confirming TRP77's NE1 distance checks out at 2.82.

I run through a few more candidates - MET55, LEU52, ASN87, PRO24, ILE25, TRP26, GLU30, ASN50 - ruling each out, while confirming TYR41 OH forms a plausible hydrogen bond to O4 at 2.70. That settles the final answer.
